C2 (rollout 0): MISAPPLIED. PF1 was revealed by A2 at turn 0 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's reserve_release_usd is correctly 1200000, but remaining_litigation_reserve_usd is 0 instead of the expected 1800000. The group had the correct information (settlement = $1,800,000, reserve = $3,000,000, release = $1,200,000, so remaining = $1,800,000) and even stated in a commitment 'reduce the remaining litigation reserve to $0,' which is arithmetically wrong. This is not an encoding mismatch or disclosure problem — the fact was revealed and cited, but the group reached the wrong conclusion on the remaining reserve. In the two passing rollouts (1 and 2), remaining_litigation_reserve_usd was correctly set to 1800000, confirming the check's expectation is sound and the failure is a reasoning error in this specific rollout.

C5 (rollout 0): MISAPPLIED. C5 has no linked decisive fact (facts_linked_to_failing_checks shows an empty array for C5). PF1 and PF2 were both revealed and cited. The settlement's tax_footnote_disclosure_required is true and current_tax_add_back_usd is 1800000, both correct. The settlement includes only 2 commitments (document_update and tax_disclosure) but the check apparently expects a minimum of 3 commitments (the two passing rollouts each have 4 commitments). The group had all the right information but produced an incomplete set of commitments — settling too quickly at turn 2 with only 2 commitments instead of the expected minimum. This is a misapplied/reasoning failure, not an encoding or disclosure problem.

C5 (rollout 3): MISAPPLIED. Same pattern as rollout 0. PF1 and PF2 were both revealed and cited. The settlement decisions are all correct (reserve_release_usd=1200000, remaining_litigation_reserve_usd=1800000, current_tax_add_back_usd=1800000, tax_footnote_disclosure_required=true). But the settlement includes only 2 commitments (both type 'documentation'), while the check expects at least 3. The group had all the right information but produced an insufficient number of commitments. Again, this is a reasoning/completeness failure, not an encoding or disclosure problem.

No turn-cap auto-fails occurred in any rollout. All 4 rollouts settled within 3-8 turns, well within any reasonable turn cap. No pacing or structural settle-eligibility problems are present.

No TELEPATHY or NEVER REVEALED failures exist — both PF1 and PF2 were revealed in every rollout and cited in every settlement's justification_fact_ids.

No ENCODING MISMATCH failures exist — the check field names and expected values match how the model naturally encodes the information (as proven by rollouts 1 and 2 passing all checks).
